I have little complaint with Voat or the culture here. I'm not one who needs to look for constant social validation or reinforcement of a fragile worldview. I don't need to be in total agreement with people to tolerate and respect them. What bothers me, though, is the rising and blatant racism. I think this has most tainted the public image of Voat and is one of its chief drags on growth. There isn't so much activity here that the natural filter of the 'hot' index is effective. Routine users will browse the 'new' index because there's just too little to see otherwise, and that leaves them fully exposed to such garbage posts. If you're not a pretty jaded individual, it's shocking. I'm not one to endorse any sort of censorship and don't think forums even need a downvoting feature. But, seriously, WTF century is this? Where the hell is this coming from? This is relegating Voat to the neglected trailer park of the Internet. A slightly more adult 4chan.

Being much older, Reddit had a certain practical advantage of emerging at a time when the Internet still required a certain sophistication to use and so was still dominated by an educated, nerdish, community. A community with roots in The Well and Computer Lib and university and Bay Area culture. Even where it leaned conservative, it was more a William F. Buckley sort of conservatism than Tea Party conservatism. So the asshole quotient was still relatively low, allowing the Reddit user base to grow before its 'new' index became so notorious and now rarely used and actively filtered. Perhaps the much greater accessibility of the contemporary internet to people of much lower sophistication has made the asshole quotient too high? Could it be that it's now no longer possible to get a new free-speech forum to critical mass before it is swamped by the compulsive negativity and raving lunacy of a deteriorating mainstream internet society? Was Reddit the product of an oasis of tolerance that now no longer exists? Has the internet reached its 'fermentation limit', now drowning in its own effluent? It's a troubling thought.
